overview: Both change allele frequencies over generations, but one is random chance and the other is driven by fitness advantage.
genZNote: Drift: random dice rolls deciding who survives. Selection: the environment actively judging your stats.

aspects.label: Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Random, chance fluctuations in allele frequency, unrelated to fitness.
aspects.valueB: Non-random process where individuals with advantageous traits survive and reproduce more.

aspects.label: Effect of Population Size
aspects.valueA: Much stronger in small populations, where chance events have a bigger relative impact.
aspects.valueB: Effective in populations of any size, though visible faster in larger ones with more variation.

aspects.label: Directionality
aspects.valueA: No consistent direction — can increase or decrease any allele, harmful or helpful.
aspects.valueB: Consistently favours alleles that improve survival and reproduction.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Founder effect after a small group colonises a new island.
aspects.valueB: Peppered moths becoming darker in polluted areas (industrial melanism).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Genetic drift has the strongest effect in small, isolated populations — classic exam link to the founder effect and bottleneck effect.
overlay.memoryTrick: Drift = random. Selection = directed by fitness.
overlay.commonMisconception: Genetic drift is not 'natural selection acting weakly' — it is a completely separate, chance-based mechanism.
